data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test is installed as an authority that the subject must consult before executing, making the test's own state a precondition for the subject's behavior. The 3-of-26 result is a consequence of compile.py's shown-to-fail-first installation creating a temporal ordering where the test's failure state was registered before the subject's guards were initialized, so 1 of 9 mutations was lost because the guard for that mutation was initialized after the failure state and inherited it as a default.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The loss would be 0/9 if the registry were cleared before each mutation","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The loss would be 9/9 if all guards were loaded after the failure state","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The effect would disappear if the guard initialization ignored pre-existing failure states","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The asymmetry would vanish if the installation order were randomized","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first ritual establishes a temporal precedence: the test's failure state is written to a shared registry before the subject's guard modules are loaded. When a guard module is loaded after the failure state exists, its initialization reads the registry and sets its default state to 'already-failing'. This default state causes the guard to skip its first check, absorbing the first mutation it encounters. The 1/9 mutation that was lost corresponds to a guard that was loaded after the failure state and encountered its first mutation before any reset, while other modules' guards were either loaded before the failure state or encountered successful mutations that reset their default.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
